page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg8i.xlarge is a high clock speed virtual server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by the x86_64 architecture featuring a dedicated 4-vCPU Intel Xeon 6462C processor operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, which supports applications requiring elevated processor frequencies alongside standard memory allocations.

This server type does not include bundled local storage or hardware GPU acceleration, requiring persistent storage needs to be addressed through attached cloud block storage volumes. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary. Without local disks, storage throughput relies strictly on network-attached storage infrastructure.

From a resource-density perspective, the high clock speed processor offers strong single-thread execution capabilities for compute-intensive tasks, balancing processing power with a general-purpose memory ratio. Tradeoffs center on the total absence of local NVMe storage and lack of included public IP addresses. Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg8i.xlarge is well tailored for workloads such as batch processing, application servers, build systems, web serving, and continuous integration pipelines that benefit from elevated CPU clock rates without necessitating dedicated accelerators.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg8i.xlarge is a high clock speed compute instance utilizing the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 6462C processor clocked at 3.3 GHz and paired with 16.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per vCPU), this server is designed for tasks requiring strong per-core performance. The configuration includes no local storage and zero GPU accelerators, meaning workloads rely on external cloud storage infrastructure, accompanied by a 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Cost efficiency is driven by high single-core compute performance within a standard 1:4 CPU-to-memory allocation, avoiding the overhead of specialized hardware. The instance suits continuous integration and delivery runners, mid-tier web serving, compilation environments, and general application workloads requiring high frequency processing without local disk dependencies.
